question.problem:
The formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence is $f(n)=10\cdot (-5)^{n}$ for $n\ge 1.$ What is the recursive formula for this sequence? Express your answer in terms of $f(n).$

$f(n+1)=$
{{field-1}}$,\,f(1)=$
{{field-2}}$,\,n\ge 1$
question.worked_solution:
The recursive formula for a geometric sequence is

$$
f(n+1)=r\cdot f(n).
$$

To complete the formula, we must determine the common ratio $r$ and state the first term $f(1).$ The first two terms are

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & =10\cdot (-5)^{1}=10\cdot (-5)=-50, \\ f(2) & =10\cdot (-5)^{2}=10\cdot 25=250.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the common ratio is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=\frac{f(2)}{f(1)}=\frac{250}{(-50)}=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the recursive formula for the geometric sequence is

$$
f(n+1)=-5f(n),\,f(1)=-50,\,n\ge 1.
$$
